# Run the code

The windows below run **R inside your browser** --nothing to install, thanks to [WebAssembly](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/) and the [quarto-live](https://r-wasm.github.io/quarto-live/) extension. Edit the code, press *Run Code*, break things, fix them.

Below you can find a familiar exercise from the Plots session:

```{webr}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(data = diamonds, aes(x = carat, y = price, color = cut)) +
  geom_point()
```

# Your turn

Complete the code to count how many diamonds there are for each `cut`, from most to least common. If you get stuck, check the hint --and only then the solution.

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_count
library(dplyr)

diamonds |>
  count(______) |>
  arrange(______)
```

::: {.hint exercise="ex_count"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="false"}
## Hint

`count()` takes the variable you want to tally. `arrange(desc(n))` sorts the tally from largest to smallest.
:::
:::

::: {.solution exercise="ex_count"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Solution

```r
library(dplyr)

diamonds |>
  count(cut) |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```
:::
:::
